theme: Expedia and Hotels.com datasets (Expedia hotel recommendation Kaggle, personalized ranking ICDM 2013, Expedia scrapers), Trivago RecSys 2019, Kayak/Skyscanner scrapers
queries_run: gh search repos "expedia hotel recommendation" --sort stars

candidates.name: Expedia Hotel Recommendations (Kaggle 2016)
candidates.what_it_holds: ~37M rows of Expedia search/click/booking logs (2013-2014), fields: user location, search destination, check-in/out dates, is_package, is_booking, hotel_cluster (100 clusters), hotel_country/market. Dozens of GitHub repos (mandalsubhajit/Kaggle--Expedia-Hotel-Recommendations, 26 stars; gouravshenoy/ExpediaHotelRecommendation, 7 stars; ~40 more found) contain only modeling notebooks — none redistribute the raw CSVs (Kaggle competition rules forbid it), so a Kaggle account/API key is required to pull the actual data. External host: kaggle.com/c/expedia-hotel-recommendations.
candidates.why_useful: Real Expedia booking-intent data with dates/destinations could inform seasonality/destination-mix patterns for gap 9 (competitor OTA volumes) and lead-time structure for gap 3 (RNPL), but the data is stale (2013-14), pre-dates current STR competitive dynamics, and requires manual Kaggle download — GitHub itself holds no data, only unusable duplicate solution code.
candidates.license: mixed (repos mostly no license; underlying Kaggle data has competition-specific terms)
candidates.size_hint: ~37M interaction rows in original Kaggle files; GitHub repos themselves are code-only (few KB)
candidates.last_activity: most recently updated fork 2025-12-03 (mandalsubhajit); original competition data unchanged since 2015

candidates.name: Personalize Expedia Hotel Searches - ICDM 2013
candidates.what_it_holds: ICDM 2013 Data Mining Cup Expedia dataset: hotel search impression logs with property price, star rating, review score, location score, promotion flag, and click/booking labels, ~10M search-result rows across ~1000 destinations. Repos found (igorpejic/personalize_expedia_hotel_searches_2013, 7 stars — code-only, requires user-supplied train.csv/test.csv path; gxanth/Learning-to-rank-with-Expedia, MIT; jlin-vt/expedia2013; 5 more near-duplicate solution repos) hold only ranking-model code (LightGBM/XGBoost learning-to-rank scripts), not the raw data.
candidates.why_useful: If ever obtained, gives granular hotel price/rating/promo fields that could sanity-check OTA pricing-competition dynamics (gap 9) and search-to-book funnel structure analogous to Airbnb's; but again 2013-vintage, Kaggle-gated, and no GitHub mirror actually carries the CSVs.
candidates.license: mixed, mostly none; gxanth/Learning-to-rank-with-Expedia is MIT (code only)
candidates.size_hint: ~10M rows in original files; GitHub repos are code-only

candidates.name: Trivago RecSys Challenge 2019 dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Trivago clickstream dataset: ~910k user sessions / ~15M interactions (clicks, filters, sort actions, impressions with price) over European hotel search sessions, released for the ACM RecSys 2019 Challenge. GitHub repo wydzik/trivago-recsyschallenge-2019 only contains data-splitting notebooks (dask_data_split.ipynb, data_split.ipynb, functions.py) that assume the user already has the official CSVs from the challenge site/Kaggle mirror — no data files are committed to the repo itself.
candidates.why_useful: A large real clickstream dataset with hotel prices and session-level search behavior across European markets in 2019; could inform methodology for search-intent-to-booking conversion or price-elasticity structure relevant to gap 9 (Expedia/Booking.com adjacent supply) and gap 2 (realized pricing proxies), but it is not committed to GitHub and is now a stale (2019) one-time competition snapshot rather than an ongoing feed.
candidates.license: none stated on wydzik repo; official dataset carries RecSys Challenge academic-use terms
candidates.time_coverage: 2019 (roughly Nov 2018-Apr 2019 session window per public challenge description)
candidates.size_hint: ~15M interaction rows / ~910k sessions (official); GitHub repo itself <1MB of scripts

candidates.name: flight-price-prediction (Kayak scraper)
candidates.what_it_holds: 55-star repo: a working Selenium-based Kayak.com scraper plus a scraped one-way flight-price dataset (city pairs, dates, prices) used to train a random forest regressor; scraper code is reusable to re-pull current Kayak fares on demand.
candidates.why_useful: A working, actively-maintained (updated 2026-09-08) non-Airbnb scraper for flight prices could be repurposed as a cheap, point-in-time-capable proxy for travel-demand/price intensity feeding gap 10 (airline/transport capacity) and cross-checking consumer travel-spend strength; scraping Kayak is not on the sanctioned-source list, so running it is a ToS decision for a human, not something to execute here.
candidates.time_coverage: point-in-time scrape at run time; historical scraped sample committed in repo (date range not specified in listing)
candidates.size_hint: small scraped CSV sample plus scraper script (~repo is a few hundred KB)

candidates.name: Kayak-Scraper (flight data library)
candidates.what_it_holds: 9-star Python scraping library that pulls flight search results (route, date, price, airline) directly from kayak.com; no data committed, method only.
candidates.why_useful: A maintained (updated 2026-04-30) general-purpose Kayak flight-data puller; same rationale as the flight-price-prediction repo for gap 10 travel-demand proxies, but purely a method with no stored data and scraping Kayak is outside sanctioned sources — flag only, do not run.

candidates.name: skyscanner-scraper (omkarcloud)
candidates.what_it_holds: Actively maintained (updated 2026-09-08) scraper/API wrapper claiming to pull Skyscanner flight search results as structured JSON (routes, prices, dates); free tier of 1,000 calls/month advertised. No historical data committed, method only.
candidates.why_useful: Another non-Airbnb, actively maintained flight-search puller relevant to gap 10 (airline capacity/traffic) and general travel-demand cross-checks; scraping Skyscanner is outside the sanctioned-source list so this is catalogued as a method only, not run.

candidates.name: trivago-scraper (Oxylabs)
candidates.what_it_holds: 33-star vendor (Oxylabs) example scraper/API wrapper for pulling live Trivago hotel search-result data (prices, hotel names, ratings) at scale; no dataset committed, demonstrates a paid-proxy-backed pull method.
candidates.why_useful: Illustrates a currently working method to pull live trivago.com hotel price comparisons across many booking sites, which could proxy short-term hotel-rate movements (gap 8/9) if a human decided to run it; commercial/proxy-dependent and off the sanctioned-source list, so flagged as method only.

candidates.name: Trivago_Classification
candidates.what_it_holds: Repo description says it models hotel booking cancellations using a "Trivago Hotel Booking dataset" and Random Forest; README references a hotel_bookings.csv but the fetched README text was truncated/incomplete and did not confirm whether the CSV is actually committed to the repo or sourced externally (likely the well-known Antonio/Almeida/Nunes Portugal hotel-bookings dataset, mislabeled as "Trivago" — that dataset is already held per CONTEXT.md).
candidates.why_useful: Possible false lead — if it is the Antonio et al. Portugal hotel-bookings dataset, it duplicates data we already hold; worth a follow-up check by the next scout before citing, since the actual data provenance could not be confirmed from the README fetch alone.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: possibly Portugal hotel-booking demand dataset (Antonio/Almeida/Nunes) already held per CONTEXT.md line 28

notes: This theme is dry on GitHub: dozens of near-duplicate Kaggle-competition solution notebooks exist for both the 2016 'Expedia Hotel Recommendations' click/booking competition and the 2013 ICDM 'Personalize Expedia Hotel Searches' ranking competition, but NONE of the ~70 repos surveyed actually commit the underlying CSVs to GitHub (Kaggle competition terms forbid redistribution) — every one requires a manual Kaggle pull, which is why every entry above is rated low and marked pointer_to_external_host rather than stored_dataset. Same story for the official Trivago RecSys 2019 Challenge dataset: repos only contain data-processing scripts assuming a pre-downloaded copy. The one area with real, currently-working, committed-method value is flight-price scrapers (Kayak, Skyscanner) as travel-demand proxies (gap 10) — several are actively maintained in 2026 — but scraping any of these sites is outside the sanctioned-source list per CONTEXT.md rules, so they are catalogued as methods only and were not run. No Hipcamp/Vrbo/Agoda/Sonder equivalents surfaced under this theme's keywords (worth a dedicated competitor-supply scout, gap 9). Used all 6 permitted `gh search repos` calls; ran out of WebSearch budget (shared session-wide quota exhausted by other scouts) before I could verify the Alexander-Kahanek repo's actual data provenance or search for a possible unofficial GitHub mirror of the Trivago RecSys 2019 CSVs — flagging for a follow-up scout with WebSearch budget remaining.
